products.what_it_changes: Removes the AER air spring and the stock damping internals and installs a pressurised closed cartridge with a coil spring in each leg and external fully variable preload. Testers: much better small-bump/square-edge absorption and front-end tracking than AER, more consistent feel, no air checks; about 3-3.5 lb heavier (slower steering feel); base valving can lack big-hit ramp-up for fast riders.
products.supporting_parts: 485 mm WP coil springs (rider weight), WP fork oil, seal kit; REP Cone Perch System fits 6500 kits; REP fork lug tool helps with heavy springs.

feedback.finding: MXA: plush over braking bumps/rocks, better corner traction; heavier; pros wanted more mid/bottom ramp-up (fixed with +30 cc and shim change).
MXA (Dec 2022): $1,299 kit + $135 springs, ~$1,500 installed; better small-bump comfort, avoids AER late-stroke spike; 3.5 lb heavier.
Keefer (KTM 450 SX-F): 6500 more front feel and small-bump absorption than Cone Valve fork; Cone Valve better under heavy braking/load. 6500 + REP valving rated better value for most riders.
Keefer (2023/24 450 SX-F): even WP base setting softer and more compliant than stock AER; REP tuning added traction.
Vital MX riders: 6500 inserts preferred by some over 7548; one rider found himself oversprung and went one rate softer with more compression.

products.caveats: WP does not publish a public setting sheet; the clicker numbers above are MXA's tested baseline, not WP's. Kit article numbers for 2023+ chassis unchanged per dealers (21-27).
